newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Airbus signs up first A3XX partners.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Airbus signs up first A3XX partners.

text.p: European planemaker Airbus Industrie on Friday signed up the first partners for its ambitious project to build an aircraft large enough to challenge Boeing 's monopoly on large-capacity commercial jets.

Airbus said it signed memoranda of understanding with Belgium's Belairbus and Fokker Aviation, a unit of Dutch engineering firm Stork NV, on the study phase of the the project, dubbed the A3XX large aircraft programme.

Airbus said the accords were signed with a view to Belairbus and Fokker becoming risk-sharing partners in the A3XX programme. They were expected to lead to a commercial agreement which would send about $2 billion in business volume toward Belairbus and Fokker, Airbus said.

The accords should help shorten the odds on Airbus' risky but potentially lucrative gamble to build the big plane. Success would firmly establish Airbus as all but equal to Boeing, while failure could be extremely costly.
Airbus estimates the development costs for the jet at $8 billion. Most analysts say it will cost more, so much more that its failure would deal Airbus' a major, long-term blow.
"It's a positive in terms of the timetable," said Emmanuel Dubois-Pelerin, analyst with S&P-ADEF in Paris. "They are obviously advancing the programme...the last question is financing."
The announcement also brightens Fokker Aviation's future, Dubois-Pelerin said.
"Every piece of work they can find is good for them because their position is so delicate," he said.
Fokker Aviation consists of the healthy aircraft component and maintenance busnesses acquired by Stork after aircraft maker Fokker NV was declared bankrupt last year.

Airbus said engineers from Fokker and Belairbus will be integrated in the A3XX programme and that the two companies would evaluate to what extent they wanted to deepen their commitment to the programme.
"This is a first step for closer cooperation between the aircraft industries of the two countries and Airbus Industrie," Airbus said in a statement.
"Participation in this phase will allow Belairbus and Fokker Aviation to evaluate the extent of their involvement in future phases of the A3XX programme."
Airbus said it was in talks with other aerospace companies around the world and hoped to split as much as 40 percent of the A3XX work content among risk-sharing partners.
The A3XX would carry about 500 passengers, considerably more than the largest version of Boeing's successful 747 series.
Both Fokker and Belairbus have been associate members of the Airbus consortium on specific aircraft programmes in the past.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
